description: Establish a working baseline before any removal. Confirm which Python runtimes/libraries are available in the (likely offline) sandbox, run the existing pytest suite to capture the starting state, and record which tests currently pass/fail/error. This creates the reference point for verifying later features do not break the retained rule-based core. No code changes in this feature.
steps: From workspace root, check Python and key libs: run 'cd python_bridge && python --version && python -c "import pandas, numpy, ta; print(pandas.__version__, numpy.__version__)"'. Note whether torch/transformers are installed (expected heavy/optional).

Attempt dependency install only if network is available: 'cd python_bridge && pip install -r requirements.txt'. If it fails due to no network, record that and proceed with whatever is preinstalled (pandas/numpy/ta/pytest are the ones the retained core needs).

Run the full suite and capture results: 'cd python_bridge && python -m pytest tests/ -v'. Record per-file pass/fail/error counts. Tests that import torch (test_models.py) or the RL agent (test_rl_agent.py) may already error if torch is missing; note that these target code being removed.
Run a focused baseline on the retained core: 'cd python_bridge && python -m pytest tests/test_backtester.py tests/test_auto_optimizer.py -v' and confirm these pass (or record exact failures).
Record the baseline summary in this feature's findings field: which tests pass, which fail, and whether network/torch are available.
